subject.title: feat: add jsonl support to memory indexer

question: Should arbitrary JSONL files from memorySearch.extraPaths become a builtin memory-core ingestion format, or should raw message logs stay outside builtin extraPaths and use QMD/session-memory/converter/plugin workflows instead?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but adding raw JSONL ingestion broadens sensitive transcript/log indexing and crosses the current Markdown-oriented builtin memory contract, so the permanent product/security boundary needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Document supported alternative
options.body: Keep builtin memory extraPaths Markdown/multimodal-only and document the QMD, session-memory, converter, or plugin workflow for raw JSONL recall.

options.title: Add native builtin JSONL
options.body: Accept JSONL as a builtin memory format and require line-aware parsing, watcher and memory_get support, tests, docs, and privacy guardrails.

options.title: Defer until memory backend direction settles
options.body: Leave this feature parked while the recommended memory backend path converges, avoiding another builtin format contract for now.

recommendation.title: Document supported alternative
recommendation.body: Keep builtin memory extraPaths Markdown/multimodal-only and document the QMD, session-memory, converter, or plugin workflow for raw JSONL recall.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already supplied the relevant keep-open analysis and is strongly connected to the memory host/runtime ownership boundary.
